files.role: contract owner (unwrap() checks presence of error property)

missed.note: Right repo, wrong file. Answered tldraw with packages/state/src/lib/Computed.ts + constants.ts (the signals library's error wrapper / UNINITIALIZED sentinel) instead of the @tldraw/utils Result type.

Repo not returned at all. RTK Query's unwrap() was hypothesised early but abandoned: the RTK source snapshot at commit b1c5130154c4 is partial (shakedown scanned only 78 files, 17 under src/), so greps for 'result.error' returned 0 hits and the lead was dropped instead of being pursued through the graph tools (case_file/manhunt), which do have the file.

calibration_comparison.verdict: Same recall as the gold-blind bare probe; slightly better precision on a smaller answer. Both halves of the anchor repo's defect were found and ranked top-4; both contract-owner citations were missed.

what_worked: substrate stakeout on the memoization symptom put packages/query-core/src/queriesObserver.ts at rank 1 on the first call; the_receipts confirmed `!this.#combinedResult` guarding `combine(input)` verbatim.
collateral_damage seeded on queriesObserver.ts returned the framework useQueries adapters, which is how preact-query/src/useQueries.ts entered the answer at all.
what_went_wrong: The two contract-owner clues were matched to plausible-but-wrong files. 'tagged pair whose tag says which arm it is' was read as TanStack Router's LoaderOutcome tuples ([SUCCESS, data] | [ERROR, error]) and React Compiler's Utils/Result.ts; the intended file was tldraw's packages/utils/src/lib/control.ts, which was never searched for because the tldraw grep was scoped to error-truthiness rather than to Result/ok/err.

'enumerates the values that have no natural ordering, handled explicitly' was matched with high confidence to TanStack DB's packages/db/src/utils/comparison.ts (isUnorderable, verbatim comment 'treat them explicitly instead of letting NaN compare unequal to everything'). That is a genuinely strong textual match and is NOT gold - a distractor the grader did not anticipate.

Time was spent hunting the failure-axis defect across jotai, zustand, xyflow, tldraw, table, redux-devtools, reselect and react-redux by grep, landing on react-redux src/components/connect.tsx (`if (!error) lastThrownError = null`) - a real instance of the same bug, but not gold. The gold failure-axis defect was in the SAME repo as the anchor (preact-query), which the anchor fold had already surfaced.
A partial source snapshot (redux-toolkit @ b1c5130154c4) was treated as evidence of absence. The correct move on 'scanned 78 files' is to switch to the graph layer, not to drop the hypothesis.
lessons: When one defect is confirmed, exhaust its own repo for the second defect before sweeping other repos - the prompt's 'spans more than one repository' was already satisfied by the citations.
shakedown reporting an implausibly small scan count is a snapshot gap, not an absence result; escalate to case_file/manhunt for that repo.
Contract-owner clues describe a TYPE, so search the type vocabulary (Result/ok/err/tagged union) in each candidate repo rather than the defect's vocabulary.
